docs.description: Case name: United Mine Workers v. Pennington Opinion filed: 1965-06-07 Docket No.: 48 Citations: • 14 L. Ed. 2d 626 • 85 S. Ct. 1585 • 381 U.S. 657 • 1965 U.S. LEXIS 2207 Case holding summaries: • Wages are at the heart of issues about which employers and unions must bargain • "Joint efforts to influence public officials do not violate the antitrust laws even though intended to eliminate competition. Such conduct is not illegal, either standing alone or as part of a broader scheme itself violative of the Sherman Act." • it is permissible for a combination of workers and their employers to petition the Secretary of Labor to take an action that adversely affects competitors • First Amendment protects concerted efforts to influence public officials • agreement to set prices of goods is not exempt • shielding from antitrust immunity any "concerted effort to influence public officials" • decreeing that antitrust laws cannot be interpreted to prohibit joint efforts to influence public officials through otherwise legal methods • "Noerr shields from the Sherman Act a concerted effort to influence public officials regardless of intent or purpose." • relying on Noerr’s protection of “effort[s] to 1 influence public officials regardless of intent or purpose” of the efforts • “Joint efforts to influence public officials do not violate the antitrust laws even though intended to eliminate competition.” • implicit exemption necessary to harmonize Sherman Act with "national policy . . . of promoting `the peaceful settlement of industrial disputes by subjecting labor-management controversies to the mediatory influence of negotiation' " • holding plaintiffs could not recover damages resulting from the state's actions • joint efforts by miners' union and large coal companies to have federal agency impose higher minimum wage for coal suppliers to TVA were immune from antitrust liability • " Noerr shields from the Sherman Act a concerted effort to influence public officials regardless of intent or purpose." • extending Noerr-Pennington immunity to efforts to influence agency decision-making, stating that "joint efforts to influence public officials do not violate the antitrust laws even though intended to eliminate competition" • joint effort by employers and union to influence public officials even though intended to eliminate competition • "because they must bargain does not mean that the agreement reached may disregard other law" • attempting to influence executive actions • labor-management agreement designed to drive competitors out of business is subject to the antitrust laws • stating that illegal pur- EMPRESS LLC v. SAN FRANCISCO 10955 poses and motivations behind petitioning do not illegalize the petitioning conduct • extending Noerr immunity to petitions of public officials • finding that the Petition Clause protects "a concerted effort to influence public officials" • " Noerr shields ... a concerted effort to influence public officials regardless of intent of purpose" • no antitrust liability for joint efforts to influence government officials or for injuries resulting from related action by government official • agreement to set prices of goods is not exempt • “Joint efforts to influence public officials do not violate the antitrust laws even though intended to eliminate competition.” • holding that immunity extends to petitioning conduct “either standing alone or as part of a broader scheme” • publicity campaign by railroad companies designed to obtain legislation adverse to trucking industry held protected under First Amendment right of access to government • noting that Noerr shielded a defendant from antitrust liability for "efforts to influence public officials . . . even though intended to eliminate competition" • agreements resulting from union-employer bargaining are not automatically exempt from Sherman Act • concerted efforts to influence public officials shielded from Sherman Act • extending Noerr protection to efforts to influence wage rates set by the Department of Labor • "Such conduct is not illegal .... The jury should have been so instructed and ... we cannot hold this lapse to be mere harmless error." • "Nothing could be clearer from the Court's opinion than that anticompetitive purpose did not illegalize the conduct there involved" • union forfeited statutory exemption where it "agree[s] with one set of employers" to eliminate competition from the industry • exemption does not apply to agreement to impose uniform industry-wide terms on employers not party to the agreement • "Joint efforts to influence public officials do not violate the antitrust laws even though intended to eliminate competition." • stating that illegal purposes and motivations behind petitioning do not illegalize the petitioning conduct • extending Noerr to joint activity to persuade administrative agency • "Joint efforts to influence public officials do not violate the antitrust laws even though intended to eliminate competition" (emphasis added) • influencing Secretary of Labor to enact labor standards • union forfeits its exemption from antitrust laws when it agrees with one set of employers to impose a wage scale on other bargaining units
